### 4. Ports

- **Game/join port:** UDP 2001 (default; players actually connect here)
- **A2S query port:** UDP 17777 (Steam server-browser query — this is the standard post-boot health-check target)
- **RCON port:** 19999 — **protocol transport is contested and NEEDS VERIFICATION BEFORE SHIPPING.** The jsknnr Docker image exposes it as TCP; but independent host docs (Terabit.io, XGamingServer) describe Arma Reforger's RCON as running "over the BattlEye RCon protocol — a UDP-based admin channel with CRC32 packet integrity." A third source (ZAP-Hosting) describes a `BEServer_x64.cfg`-based setup that is actually Arma 3's legacy BattlEye config pattern, likely miscopied onto a Reforger page. I could not resolve this against the primary Bohemia wiki (blocked). **Do not build a raw-TCP-connect health check or a live RCON client against port 19999 until this is confirmed** — recommend using the UDP A2S query on 17777 for post-boot health verification instead, since that one is corroborated consistently across every source with no contradiction.

**GAME_PORT recommendation:** `{ port: 17777, protocol: "udp" }` for health-check, with a join-port override of `{ port: 2001, protocol: "udp" }` for the actual player-facing port.

Two notes on this draft vs. the Mordhau/V Rising precedent:

### 9. Mods

Arma Reforger does **not** use Steam Workshop or mod.io — it uses **Bohemia's own official Workshop platform** (`reforger.armaplatform.com/workshop`), which the dedicated server pulls mods from directly (not via Steam) when mod IDs/versions are listed in the server config. This does **not** map onto any existing Nxeon `SOURCE_LABEL` (`modrinth, spigotmc, hangar, curseforge, steam_workshop, umod, github, nexus, thunderstore, codefling, mod_io`) — **a new source key (e.g. `bohemia_workshop`) would need to be added** if Nxeon wants a mod browser UI for this game.

There is a well-documented third-party public API — **ReforgerMods.net** (https://reforgermods.net/) — that indexes Workshop mods/scenarios and server listings, with a free tier and paid keys for heavier use; it's already used by real community tooling (Old Guard Revival, 55th MEU) to power mod-list management and Discord bots. This is a realistic, low-risk integration path for a future "browse & attach official mods" feature, distinct from ingesting mods directly from Bohemia (no public download API confirmed for that side — only the Script API's `SCR_WorkshopItem` interface, which is for in-game/client use, not a server-side bulk-download API).

## SCUM

### 1. Is it really self-hostable / resellable?

**Yes, but only via Wine — no Linux-native server binary exists, and this has a real, disclosed anti-cheat trade-off.**

- Base game Steam app: `513710` (this is what SteamCharts/player-count tools use)
- **Dedicated server tool app: `3792580`** — confirmed independently by the official Scum Wiki ("Use app id 3792580 for SCUM server" — https://scum.wiki.gg/wiki/Scum_Dedicated_server_setup), by SteamCharts itself listing a distinct "SCUM Server" page at `steamcharts.com/app/3792580`, and by multiple community server-manager tools (WindowsGSM.SCUM, wickstudio/scum-server-setup). Anonymous SteamCMD login works fine for it.
- **The server binary (`SCUMServer.exe`) is Windows-only, 64-bit.** Every actively maintained Linux hosting project for SCUM (EvilOlaf, melle2, VelocipedeRider, jasonlcsdev) runs it under **Wine**, not natively — strong convergent confirmation there is no native Linux build.
- **Anti-cheat:** SCUM uses **BattlEye**, not Easy Anti-Cheat (one old 2018-era Valve/Proton GitHub issue thread title mentions "EAC" for this app, which appears to predate a later switch to BattlEye, or was simply a misnomer at the time — current, actively-maintained docs and every current Docker image reference BattlEye exclusively). BattlEye's kernel-level hooks **do not function under Wine**, so **any Wine-hosted SCUM server must run with BattlEye disabled** via the game's own official `-nobattleye` launch parameter (documented directly in the game's own dedicated-server setup guide, not a fan hack). This is standard, disclosed, industry-wide practice: PingPerfect, BisectHosting, GGServers, and Streamline Servers all publish "how to disable BattlEye on your SCUM server" knowledge-base articles for exactly this reason. **This is not a silent workaround — it's an accepted trade-off the entire hosting industry makes for this specific game, but Nxeon should disclose it plainly to buyers** ("this server type doesn't run with anti-cheat enabled") rather than bury it, since players connecting from vanilla Windows clients to a BattlEye-disabled server have no anti-cheat protection.

**Verdict: viable and already standard industry practice, conditional on Nxeon explicitly disclosing the anti-cheat trade-off to buyers (an honesty/trust issue, not a technical blocker).**

Sources: [scum.wiki.gg dedicated server setup](https://scum.wiki.gg/wiki/Scum_Dedicated_server_setup), [ValveSoftware/Proton issue #1248](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/Proton/issues/1248), [BisectHosting: How to Disable Battleye](https://help.bisecthosting.com/hc/en-us/articles/47766585881371-How-to-Disable-Battleye-on-a-SCUM-Server), [PingPerfect: How to disable BattlEye](https://pingperfect.com/knowledgebase/1230/SCUM--How-to-disable-BattlEye.html)

### 2. Real Docker image

| Image | Env-var coverage | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **`melle2/scum-dedicated-server`** (repo `melle2/scum-ds`) | `GAME_MAX_PLAYER`, `GAME_SERVER_PORT`, `GAME_UPDATE`, `GAME_NO_BATTLEYE` | Ubuntu 24.04 + Wine 11.0; explicit volume split (`/scum` binaries, `/scum_saved` world data/config, Steam metadata separate); README last updated per Docker Hub "4 months ago" note; explicitly documents the BattlEye Wine-compatibility fix ("pre-configured with Wine libraries to pass integrity checks") |
| **`EvilOlaf/scum`** | `GAMEPORT`, `QUERYPORT`, `ADDITIONALFLAGS=-nobattleye`, memory-watchdog vars | Debian Trixie + Wine 11.0; explicitly a fork/rewrite of an older `j0s0n/scum-wine` image "fixing update/restart issues" — implies active, recent maintenance |
| `VelocipedeRider/scum-server-wine` | Arch-based, less documented | Narrower audience (Arch-specific) |
| `jasonlcsdev/scum-server-docker` | Minimal docs found | Lower confidence |

**Critical finding, most important thing in this section:** **neither `melle2/scum-ds` nor `EvilOlaf/scum` exposes server name, password, or difficulty/game-mode via docker env vars.** Both explicitly punt those to the mounted `ServerSettings.ini` file inside the persisted save volume (`/scum_saved` for melle2). **This is structurally the same shape as Nxeon's existing "The Isle" pattern (config lives in a mounted file, not `-e` flags) — not the Mordhau/V-Rising env-var pattern.** If Nxeon's UI presents "Server Name" or "Server Password" fields for SCUM and only wires them to a `docker -e` flag, **those fields will silently do nothing — this is exactly the V Rising bug's failure mode, just one layer up (file-write vs. env-var, instead of wrong env-var name).** The FamilySchema fields for those need a real templated-file-render step in the worker (writing into the mounted `ServerSettings.ini`), not just `envKey` mapping. **Flagging this explicitly: this is the single highest-risk item in this whole report for SCUM.**

Recommendation: use **`melle2/scum-ds`** for its clean env/volume split and explicit BattlEye-under-Wine handling, but budget real engineering time for an `ServerSettings.ini` template-writer, not just env-var passthrough.

**Docker-env-backed (verified against two independent image READMEs):**

| Env var (melle2 image) | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `GAME_MAX_PLAYER` | Max players (up to 128) | 64 |
| `GAME_SERVER_PORT` | Steam query port | 7779 |
| `GAME_UPDATE` | Auto-update on boot | false |
| `GAME_NO_BATTLEYE` | Disable BattlEye (required for Wine) | false — **should default true/on for Nxeon given #1 above** |

**File-backed (`ServerSettings.ini`, NOT env vars) — and here I found a real, unresolved discrepancy that is exactly the class of risk this project is trying to prevent:**

- One source (XGamingServer docs) states the literal keys are unprefixed: `ServerName`, `Password`, `MaxPlayers`.
- A second source (RespawnHost wiki) states the literal keys carry a `scum.` prefix: `scum.ServerName`, `scum.ServerPassword`, `scum.MaxPlayers`, `scum.MaxPing`, and notes "some versions use INI sections like `[SCUM.ItemSpawning]` instead."
- Two direct-fetch attempts at the more authoritative-looking pages (scum.fandom.com/wiki/Server_Settings, gghost.games's dedicated ini guide) were blocked (HTTP 402/403).

**I cannot verify which literal key form is correct. THIS NEEDS VERIFICATION BEFORE SHIPPING** — the fix is trivial (spin up one real SCUM dedicated server via the free anonymous SteamCMD app `3792580`, let it generate its own `ServerSettings.ini`, and read the literal keys) but must be done with a real running server, not by trusting either secondary source, precisely because this is the same failure mode that caused the V Rising incident (config `key` not matching what the game engine actually reads).

Difficulty/game-mode: no specific field name was confirmed for this at all in the time available — SCUM's settings file reportedly has 400+ values across sections (General, World, Respawn, Vehicles, Damage, Features) per RespawnHost's own description, and no single "difficulty" toggle was located. **Mark this whole area NEEDS VERIFICATION BEFORE SHIPPING.**

RCON/admin-password equivalent: **there is no native RCON at all** (see #4/#5). Admin access is via Steam64-ID whitelist in a separate `ServerSettingsAdminUsers.ini`, plus in-game `#`-prefixed chat commands — not a password-based remote console.

Sources: [XGamingServer SCUM server-config docs](https://xgamingserver.com/docs/scum/server-config), [RespawnHost SCUM configuration wiki](https://respawnhost.com/en/wiki/games/scum/scum-configuration/), [dustbowl.games SCUM setup](https://dustbowl.games/knowledgebase/scum-dedicated-server-setup)

### 4. Ports

No TCP port exists at all in the official binary — everything is UDP:

- **Join/game port:** UDP 7777 (configurable via `-port=`)
- **Raw socket:** UDP 7778 (port+1)
- **Steam query/server-browser port:** UDP 7779 (port+2) — this is what `melle2`'s `GAME_SERVER_PORT` env var controls, and the most reliable target for a post-boot health check.

**RCON: does not natively exist.** I found one lower-quality wiki table (scum.wiki.gg's server-setup page) claiming "TCP 7777... RCON for remote console access (optional)," but a purpose-built third-party tool whose entire reason for existing is to *add* RCON to SCUM — **SCUM Server Automation (scumsa.com)** — explicitly states: *"The SCUM dedicated server ships without an RCON protocol — there is no port to connect an RCON client to, and classic RCON tools simply don't work with SCUM."* I'm treating that as the more credible, internally-consistent source (it would be pointless for that tool to exist if native RCON worked) and **disregarding the wiki's TCP-7777-RCON claim as inaccurate/outdated.**

**GAME_PORT recommendation:** `{ port: 7779, protocol: "udp" }` for health-check, join-port override `{ port: 7777, protocol: "udp" }`.

Sources: [scumsa.com RCON docs](https://scumsa.com/docs/reference/rcon) (fetched successfully), [scum.wiki.gg server setup](https://scum.wiki.gg/wiki/Scum_Dedicated_server_setup)

```
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && mkdir -p /opt/scum && chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/scum && docker run -d --name scum --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 30 -p 7777:7777/udp -p 7778:7778/udp -p 7779:7779/udp -e GAME_MAX_PLAYER='64' -e GAME_SERVER_PORT='7779' -e GAME_UPDATE='true' -e GAME_NO_BATTLEYE='true' -v /opt/scum:/scum -v /opt/scum-saved:/scum_saved melle2/scum-dedicated-server:latest
```

`ServerName`/`ServerPassword` are deliberately **not** in this `-e` list — per #2/#3/#5, they require the worker to write into `/opt/scum-saved/.../ServerSettings.ini` after container start, using whichever literal key form is confirmed correct. Shipping this setupScript as-is with a UI that promises "set your server name" but only sets docker env vars would recreate the exact bug this project exists to prevent.

### 9. Mods

**Thin and unstable — do not oversell this.** SCUM has no Steam Workshop and no mod.io integration. The real modding home is **Nexus Mods** (~144 files as of a late-July-2026 snapshot), which **is already one of Nxeon's supported `SOURCE_LABEL` keys (`nexus`)** — so technically no new source type is needed. However:

- Most SCUM mods on Nexus are **client-side only** (UI/QoL/texture tweaks via a community "Scum Mod Manager" desktop tool) — not the server-hosted content-pack model Nxeon's mod system is presumably built around (e.g., Rust/Minecraft-style server-applied mods).
- The modding pipeline is actively unstable at the game-developer level: in late April 2026 Gamepires broke the community's modding workflow by neutralizing the `-fileopenlog` launch parameter the community relied on, then partially restored `.pak` loading support on **May 7, 2026**. This is a moving target, not a stable platform to build a Nxeon feature on top of right now.
- Mods can also interact badly with BattlEye when it's enabled — largely moot for Nxeon's Wine-hosted case since BattlEye is disabled there anyway, but worth knowing.

**Recommendation: do not build a SCUM mod-browser feature for the initial launch.** If demand emerges later, it maps to the existing `nexus` source label with no new plumbing needed — just don't promise mod support in initial marketing copy.

Sources: [Nexus Mods SCUM "Our Focus For 2026"](https://www.nexusmods.com/scum/news/15433), [Nexus Mods SCUM AllowMods](https://www.nexusmods.com/scum/mods/25), [Nexus Mods SCUM Mod Manager](https://www.nexusmods.com/scum/mods/138)

### 10. SEO/content angle

**Realistic, and demand is real (5 major hosts already selling it)**, but the honest content angle here is narrower than Arma Reforger's because two of the obvious selling points (deep mod support, RCON-based remote admin) genuinely don't exist for this game right now. Honest, defensible selling points:

- Real, disclosed anti-cheat trade-off messaging — most competitor pages bury the BattlEye-disable requirement in a support-KB article rather than the sales page; being upfront about it ("runs on Linux, which means BattlEye is off by default — here's what that means for you") is a genuine differentiator built on honesty rather than a fabricated one.
- Real slot/RAM/CPU-clock transparency (SCUM is explicitly RAM-hungry per official minimums — leading with real numbers instead of "optimized performance" filler is credible).
- World-save backup reliability, since SCUM's persistent world state is valuable to players and is a real, verifiable feature (mounted `/scum_saved` volume) rather than a marketing claim.

Do **not** claim mod support, one-click RCON admin, or a "workshop" for SCUM in launch copy — none of those are true yet, and claiming them would be exactly the kind of unverified/false claim this whole research task exists to prevent.
